claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has been reported in a hierarchical heterostructured state featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A sequential hybrid framework can use outputs from targeted computational simulations as input features for a machine-learning model.
The multilevel chemical fluctuations and heterointerfaces mediate the relationship between atomistic simulation features and macroscopic mechanical responses.
Simulation-driven identification of key atomic-level features reduces the complexity of the prediction problem.
Training a machine-learning model on simulation-derived atomic features captures local and long-range interaction effects better than simulation or machine learning used separately.
The hybrid framework will improve predictions of Young's modulus, yield strength, and toughness for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
The hybrid framework will reduce mechanical-property prediction errors by approximately 10–20% relative to traditional computational methods.
The hybrid framework will reduce required computation time by approximately one order of magnitude.
Extensive first-principles calculations and CALPHAD have high computational demands.
Existing standalone computational and machine-learning methods have limited accuracy for predicting fracture properties.
The framework may become unreliable when unforeseen microstructural evolution or phase changes lie outside the training-data domain.
The framework may become unreliable when chemical fluctuations or heterostructural complexity differ substantially from those represented during model development.
Variation in processing and experimental conditions may affect the realized prediction accuracy and efficiency.
A blinded prospective benchmark can compare preregistered predictions with tensile and fracture measurements on newly prepared HfNbTiVAl10 samples.

The hypothesis is designated as falsified if any predicted mechanical property differs from experiment by more than 15% or if computation time is reduced by less than fivefold relative to the baseline.
